---
title: "Runway threshold crossing"
description: "How OPDI finds the moment a landing aircraft passes over the runway threshold (xing-runway-threshold)."
---

## In one sentence

`xing-runway-threshold` is the moment a landing aircraft passes over the
**runway threshold**, the start of the part of the runway that may be used
for landing, a few seconds before it touches down.

## What it needs

- An arrival **runway pass** (see
  [Take-off and landing times](take-off-landing.qmd#runway-pass-method)).
- Reports in the 60 s before the aircraft enters the runway area, because the
  report short of the threshold lies outside the runway itself.
- The height above the ground, measured from the track's own ground altitude
  (see [Take-off and landing times](take-off-landing.qmd#height-above-the-ground)).

## How it is computed

1. Take the reports of the arrival pass and those of the 60 s before it.
2. For each report, compute its distance along the runway centre line from
   the threshold of the landing direction: negative before the threshold,
   positive after it.
3. A crossing is the moment this distance changes sign, inbound. A dead band
   of 0.05 NM (about 300 ft) either side of the threshold confirms the
   crossing, so a report sitting on the line cannot trigger it twice. The time
   and position are interpolated in a straight line between the two reports
   either side of the threshold itself.
4. Keep one crossing per landing: the last inbound crossing of the pass, and
   only when the aircraft is at most 300 ft above the ground there. On a
   3° approach an aircraft crosses the threshold about 50 ft above it. A low
   pass, an overflight or a circuit over the runway gives no event.

## Based on

- Developed for OPDI, with the same crossing method as the flight-level and
  distance-circle crossings (a dead band, then interpolation).
- The [A-CDM Implementation Manual](../resources.qmd#ref-acdm-manual) has no threshold
  milestone; its landing (milestone 6) is the touchdown. The code `T16` in
  `info.milestone` is a label in the PRU flight diagram, not the manual's number; see
  [Milestones of a flight](index.qmd#milestones-of-a-flight).
- Thresholds from [OurAirports](../resources.qmd#ref-ourairports).

## What is published

Event type `xing-runway-threshold`, with position, altitude,
`distance_flown_nm` and `time_passed_s`. Its `info` holds `apt_icao`,
`runway`, `runway_bearing_deg`, `traversal_class` (`arrival`), `align_deg`,
`max_gs_kt`, `milestone` and `height_reference` (see the
[Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

Do not confuse it with `entry-threshold` and `exit-threshold`, which are
[airport surface events](surface-events.qmd) of aircraft on the ground near
the threshold markings.

## Use cases

- **Arrival flow over the threshold**: count crossings per runway and
  quarter-hour for the landing rate actually achieved.
- **Spacing between arrivals**: the time between the crossings of two
  consecutive arrivals on one runway.
- **Flare and touchdown**: `ALDT` minus `xing-runway-threshold` of the same
  flight, when `ALDT` comes from the runway pass (`info.method` = `acdm`).

## Limitations

Missing when the aircraft was not received in the last minute before the
runway or when its last report on approach was too high. See
[Limitations: runway events](../limitations.qmd#lim-runway).

## Availability and accuracy

No record gives the threshold crossing itself. It is compared with the
recorded landing time, a few seconds later.
